attempted_claim: Prove or disprove the following edge fluctuation law: for Aztec diamonds of order N with fixed positive 3x2-periodic edge weights with generic values, at a generic smooth (non-cusp, non-tangency) point of the outer frozen-rough arctic curve identified by the explicit limit-shape/spectral-curve equation, the centered height function and associated top non-intersecting-path particle, rescaled with tangential scale N^{2/3} and fluctuation scale N^{1/3} about the explicit arctic location with explicit nondegenerate curvature constants obtained from the double-contour Kasteleyn inverse action function, converge to the Airy2 process with GUE Tracy-Widom one-point marginals; parameter scope is all fixed generic positive 3x2-periodic weights and every generic smooth frozen-rough boundary point; a complete answer is a rigorous proof of the stated Airy2/Tracy-Widom limit with the stated exponents and explicit centering, or a rigorous disproof by establishing a different scaling limit, different limiting law, or proof that no such universal limit exists.
claim_type: prove-or-disprove scaling limit to universal process
decisive_failure: The lane produced only a bounded numeric obstruction check (Newton polygon, genus bound, torus gap) for one generic 3x2 weight draw; it supplies no uniform analytic steepest-descent estimates, no Airy2 convergence, and no disproof. Literature conclusions rest on field knowledge recorded in the worklog rather than a formal proof search, and no independently valuable emergent result was found.
